newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds edge lower, reflecting U.S. mkts.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds edge lower, reflecting U.S. mkts.

text.p: Argentine bonds were lower in the late morning Thursday as the market continued to suffer the impact of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress.
A strong U.S. January durable goods report released Thursday added to the negative tone in the U.S. Treasuries market and that in turn weighed on the local market.
However, traders did not yet think there was a turnaround in the still strong underlying tone in the Argentine market.
"The rally will calm down a little but prices will move slowly higher," said an analyst at a foreign bank.
He said spread levels still indicated there was room for higher Argentine bond prices.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 1/4 to 91-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.05 to 126.55.
Another trader predicted strong buyer interest would emerge again around the 91 level on the FRB.
